# E102 -- Finland National Brand Identity Guidelines

## Metadata
- **Brand:** Suomi -- Finland (National Brand)
- **Industry:** Nation Branding / Government
- **Year:** 2024 (Version 1.0)
- **Pages:** 67
- **Source file:** `72fc7c7bf4ab5bdaef0cb27d1e8e5252.pdf`
- **Created with:** Adobe InDesign 20.0

## Brand Strategy
- Limited strategic section; focuses on identity execution rather than deep brand strategy
- Core brand attributes: reliable, quirky, sympathetic
- Bilingual identity: "Suomi" retained in all language versions as a "curiosity" element
- Brand toolbox website: toolbox.finland.fi for assets, presentations, images, videos, infographics
- Co-branding scenarios well-defined for partner organizations

## Logo
- Bilingual logotype: "Suomi" (top) + "Finland" (bottom), reflecting bilingual country identity
- Language versions available: "Suomi" always retained, lower element changes per language
- Logo proportions tied to Finnish flag proportions; space between elements equals flag's horizontal line
- Clear space: equal to height of "Finland" text on every side
- Minimum size: 8mm / 20px height
- Primary placement: upper left corner; alternative upper right
- Primary color usage: white and blue (Finland Blue / Finland White)
- Secondary color and image overlay usage defined
- Illustrative usage permitted with more flexibility
- Detailed incorrect usage examples provided

## Typography
- **Custom typeface:** Finlandica -- designed specifically for the Finland Brand Identity, open source/free to use
- **Finlandica Headline:** condensed, distinctive letterforms for headlines only; 9 weights (100-900) + italics
- **Finlandica Text:** wider, simpler, rounder proportions for body text; 9 weights + italics
- Hierarchy example: Overline (Finlandica Text Medium, 9pt, +100 tracking), Title (Headline Light & Medium, 50pt), Body (Text Regular, 12/16pt)
- "Plain Style" OpenType feature (Stylistic Set 01) for sleek headline variant
- Extensive OpenType features: ligatures, uppercase alternates, tabular/oldstyle figures, fractions, superscript/subscript
- 313 Latin-script languages supported
- Basic use recommendation: Regular, Italic, Bold, Bold Italic from both families
- Fallback: Noto typeface for languages Finlandica doesn't support

## Color
- Primary colors: Finland Blue, Finland White
- Supporting colors available for advanced layouts
- Black and white version only when no color is in use
- Color usage tightly integrated with flag symbol

## Graphics / Illustration
- Flag of Finland symbol as core graphic element -- used alongside logo, never standalone
- Flag symbol has its own clear space (equal to height of single white area on flag) and minimum size rules (8mm/20px)
- Outlined flag version only on white background

## Photography
- Dedicated imagery chapter (Chapter 2, p. 50+)
- Photo credits noted (Julia Kivela, Yiping Feng & Ling Ouyang)

## Applications
- Chapter 3: Grids & Layouts (p. 54+)
- Chapter 4: Best Practice Applications (p. 58+)
- Co-branding scenarios: partner logo placement rules, multi-partner name placement
- Partner names written in Finlandica Text as primary choice

## Tone of Voice
- "Honest, quirky, human"
- Brief mention: "We want everybody to know Finland is reliable, quirky and sympathetic"
- Tone section is minimal (single page) -- this is primarily a visual identity guideline

## Outliers / Unique Elements
- Custom open-source typeface (Finlandica) designed specifically for the national brand -- rare for country branding
- Bilingual logo concept with "Suomi" as a permanent curiosity element across all language versions
- Flag-as-graphic-element system with strict proportional relationship to logotype
- Extremely detailed OpenType feature documentation (ligatures, fractions, currency symbols, arrows, mathematical symbols)
- 313-language support list included -- reflects Finland's international brand ambition
- Online toolbox (toolbox.finland.fi) as a self-service brand asset platform

## Quality Score
**4/5** -- Thorough visual identity system with exceptional typographic depth (custom typeface with full OpenType documentation). Strong logo and flag symbol rules. Minor deduction: brand strategy and tone of voice sections are very thin compared to the visual system. The guide prioritizes execution over strategic foundation.
